groups.name: Start here
groups.intro: If you have never read the Bible, or never been told how it came to be, begin with these.

guides.title: What the Bible Is
guides.summary: A library of sixty-six books in two testaments and three languages: what is in it, how it is arranged, and how Jewish, Protestant, Catholic, and Orthodox Bibles differ.

guides.title: How the Books Were Chosen
guides.summary: How the Old and New Testaments came to contain the books they do, why some Bibles include the Apocrypha, and what the early church looked for in a book.

guides.title: How We Got the Old Testament
guides.summary: From scribes to the Masoretes, the Dead Sea Scrolls, the Septuagint, and the other ancient witnesses: how the Hebrew Bible reached us and how reliable it is.

guides.title: How We Got the New Testament
guides.summary: Papyri, great codices, thousands of manuscripts, and the editions behind modern Bibles: what the differences are and what they do and do not change.

guides.title: Why Translations Differ
guides.summary: Word-for-word and thought-for-thought, the history of the English Bible, and how to read small capitals, brackets, and footnotes.

guides.title: Chapters, Verses, and References
guides.summary: Who added chapter and verse numbers, how to read a reference, and where Hebrew and English Bibles number verses differently.

groups.name: How to read each kind of writing
groups.intro: Much misreading of the Bible is reading one kind of writing as if it were another. These guides show how each works.

guides.title: Reading the Stories
guides.summary: How biblical narrative works: the narrator's restraint, repetition, type-scenes, and why the heroes are rarely models.

guides.title: Reading the Law
guides.summary: Case law and command, the covenant setting, the ancient law codes around Israel, and how Christians have related the Law to Christ.

guides.title: Reading Hebrew Poetry
guides.summary: Parallelism, imagery, acrostics, the kinds of psalms, and a glossary of the psalm headings.

guides.title: Reading the Wisdom Books
guides.summary: Proverbs, Job, and Ecclesiastes: what a proverb is and is not, and how the three books argue with each other.

guides.title: Reading the Prophets
guides.summary: Who the prophets were, the forms they used, prediction and fulfillment, and how to read an oracle in its own time.

guides.title: Reading Apocalyptic
guides.summary: Daniel and Revelation in the family of ancient apocalypses: visions, symbols, numbers, and the main schools of interpretation.

guides.title: Reading the Gospels
guides.summary: Ancient biography, four portraits of one Jesus, how the first three Gospels relate, and how John differs.

guides.title: Reading the Parables
guides.summary: What a parable is, how Jesus used them, and the history of reading them from allegory to the present.

guides.title: Reading the Letters
guides.summary: The ancient letter, rhetoric and diatribe, reading someone else's mail, and household codes.

guides.title: Reading Genealogies and Lists
guides.summary: Why the Bible keeps records of names and numbers, what they did for their first readers, and what they teach now.

groups.name: The world of the Bible
groups.intro: Reference tables and background the biblical writers took for granted.

guides.title: Between the Testaments
guides.summary: From Nehemiah to Jesus: Persians, Alexander, the Ptolemies and Seleucids, the Maccabees, the Hasmoneans, Rome, and Herod.

guides.title: Pharisees, Sadducees, and Others
guides.summary: The Jewish groups and institutions of Jesus' day: Pharisees, Sadducees, Essenes, Zealots, Samaritans, scribes, the Sanhedrin, the temple, and the synagogue.

guides.title: The Kings of Israel and Judah
guides.summary: Every king of the united and divided kingdoms with approximate dates, the prophets who spoke to them, and the empires around them.

guides.title: The Empires Around Israel
guides.summary: Egypt, Assyria, Babylon, Persia, Greece, and Rome: when each ruled and where each touches the biblical story.

guides.title: The Herods and the Roman Governors
guides.summary: The Herodian family and the Roman officials who governed Judea in the New Testament era.

guides.title: Weights, Measures, and Money
guides.summary: Cubits, shekels, talents, denarii, and the rest, with modern equivalents and what they meant in daily life.

guides.title: The Calendar and Festivals
guides.summary: The Hebrew months, the Sabbath and the pilgrim festivals, the Day of Atonement, and the later feasts of Purim and Hanukkah.

guides.title: Offerings, Priests, and Purity
guides.summary: The five offerings of Leviticus, the priesthood, clean and unclean, and why the sacrificial system matters for reading the New Testament.
